From a temperature prototype
to parallel weather inference
CE436   Discrete-Time Signal Processing and Applications

Our project forecasts temperature, pressure, humidity, wind speed, and wind direction three hours ahead. We will explain the extension from our original temperature model, the parallel hardware, and the evidence from simulation and the DE2 board.

Hourly observations become a forecast
three hours ahead
At noon: use known history to predict 15:00

The timestamps belong to the data. Replaying hourly observations quickly does not change the forecast horizon. The FPGA performs inference with fixed coefficients; it does not wait three hours or train the model. We read the result on the host through JTAG.

use separate time periods
NASA POWER   Ho Chi Minh City   Hourly observations in UTC

title: Each channel learns from seven past values

text:
Each channel learns from seven past values
of the same variable
Source: weather_v2/models/model.json; temperature and humidity select ridge penalty 1
x̂(t + 3) = bias + Σ wₖ x(t − ℓₖ)
Seven weights and one bias per channel

Each output uses its own history. Humidity and pressure do not jointly predict temperature in this selected model. Each arithmetic channel has seven weights and a bias. Ridge regularization penalizes coefficient size during fitting; it does not add an iterative learning algorithm to the FPGA.

title: Cosine and sine keep nearby wind directions

text:
Cosine and sine keep nearby wind directions
close across the zero-degree boundary

Ordinary subtraction makes these nearby directions look far apart. The host encodes each input angle as cosine and sine. The FPGA predicts the two components, then a 16-step iterative CORDIC reconstructs the angle. A zero component pair has an undefined-direction flag.

Fixed-point rules make the reference
and RTL calculations comparable
Source: weather_v2/rtl/weather_ar_channel.v; C++ reference; worked example in report
Arithmetic shift by 14, then saturation and range limits

The binary point is a scaling convention. We preserve product precision and accumulate before shifting. Negative fractions use floor scaling, followed by the specified limits. The C++ reference follows those same rules, so a mismatch indicates an implementation difference rather than a weather forecast error.

title: Six lanes run in parallel, with one multiplier

text:
Six lanes run in parallel, with one multiplier
reused across each lane’s seven terms
42 products per frame, distributed over time

Parallelism is across the six channels. Each lane reuses one multiplier over its seven terms. The design therefore does not contain 42 simultaneous multipliers. History advances only when a frame is accepted. The wrapper aligns the scalar results with the reconstructed direction.

The full forecast takes 40 cycles,
with a new eligible frame every 23 cycles
Source: weather_system_speed.v; tb_weather.sv; RTL post-edge observation convention

First forecast: accepted frame 25
JTAG replay has additional host overhead

Latency and acceptance interval are different. A result takes 40 cycles, but eligible frames can enter 23 cycles apart. The first 24 accepted frames fill history. The 25th can generate the first forecast. An idle clock does not represent another hour or shift the stored sequence.

Verification checks values, transaction order
and timing through implementation
Reset cancellation and repeated history warm-up explain the RTL counts.

We check output values, order, valid timing, stalls, range limits, and reset cancellation. Resets require fresh history and cancel pending work; the RTL count cannot be explained by subtracting 24 only once. The accepted SDF run covers the predictor core at a 20 ns period. It is not a full timing simulation of the proprietary JTAG transport.

title: The selected models beat both simple

text:
The selected models beat both simple
baselines on the chronological test set
Lower MAE is better. Direction: non-calm targets, ideal angle decoding of quantized components.

Lower mean absolute error is better. Persistence repeats the latest observation. The diurnal baseline repeats yesterday at the target hour. The selected models beat both on this 2025 test set. Each chart has its own unit and scale. Scalars use 8757 targets. Direction uses 8593 targets with wind speed at least 0.5 m/s and ideal atan2 of quantized components. CORDIC conversion is checked separately. Source: versions/weather_v2/reports/metrics.csv. Planned time: 55 seconds.

The fitted weather-speed JTAG build
meets the 50 MHz timing constraint
Source: native Quartus screenshots; JTAG_IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md; uninstrumented build
4,571 registers     12 nine-bit multiplier elements     SignalTap excluded

These numbers include the board JTAG wrapper and exclude SignalTap instrumentation. Twelve nine-bit multiplier elements correspond to the six full multipliers allocated here. The board was tested at 50 MHz. The 79.74 MHz figure is a fitted timing estimate, not a physical clock sweep.

Physical replay checked 104 forecasts
and SignalTap captured a valid transaction
Source: weather_speed_physical_replay.txt; weather_speed.stp; decoded capture CSV
PASS PHYSICAL JTAG weather_speed: inputs=128 forecasts=104
41 capture intervals; 40-cycle RTL latency under the post-edge convention.

The first 24 inputs fill history, leaving 104 forecasts from 128 frames. Scalar and component outputs agreed with the fixed-point reference, and the angle passed the permitted tolerance. SignalTap captured a physical prediction transaction. Its raw edge separation is 41 acquisition intervals; the RTL's documented post-edge latency is 40 cycles. We retain the native STP and decoded CSV so this can be inspected.

title: The demonstrated system uses recorded data

text:
The demonstrated system uses recorded data
and fixed coefficients
Source: implementation scope and retained physical evidence, October 2026

Recorded inputs over JTAG
Five forecast quantities
50 MHz physical replay

Live data acquisition
Other locations and years
Measured electrical power
Rainfall probability remains outside the implemented targets.

The current evidence is for recorded inputs at one location. It does not establish live sensor operation or rainfall probability. We have not measured electrical power or the board's maximum operating frequency. Hourly forecasting does not require sub-microsecond execution; this project demonstrates a verified hardware implementation and its scheduling.

The original temperature model used
a seasonal anchor and two corrections
T̂(t + 3) = T(t − 21) + a Δdaily + b Δrecent + c

Δdaily = T(t) − T(t − 24)
Δrecent = T(t) − T(t − 3)
Temperature test MAE: 0.538017 °C in the prototype; 0.507906 °C in the current model.
